To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) An RNA linked DNA fragment has been isolated from the T7 DNA replicating system.
an RNA linked DNA species has been isolated from bacteriophage T 7 infected cells and that this molecule binds almost exclusively with the R strand of the T7 genome.
an RNA-DNA molecule has been isolated that contains an RNA linked deoxypolymucleotide chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which DNA replication is initiated.
the isolation and characterization of a DNA-RNA linked molecule which may be the first product in the initiation of DNA synthesis in T7 infected cells.
the isolation, characterization and possible function of an RNA linked deoxypolymucleotide chain which has been isolated during the initiation phase of T7 DNA synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RNA linked DNA molecules described here are intermediates in the initiation of T7 DNA replication, and that the RNA is covalently linked to the DNA by a phosphodiester linkage.
the DNA-RNA molecule isolated is a primer molecule for the initiation of T7 DNA replication.

the RNA molecule is covalently linked to a deoxyribonucleotide chain, that it is complementary to the R strand, and that the 5' end of the RNA is attached to the 3' end of the deoxyribonuleotide chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have isolated a ribonucleoprotein complex which contains RNA covalently bound to a deoxyribonucleotide chain.
we have isolated a molecule that contains a ribopolynucieotide linked to a DNA molecule.
we have isolated a ribonucleic acid covalently attached by a 5’-3’ linkage to a deoxyribonucleic acid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this RNA linked DNA molecule is a good candidate for the initiation primer.
the RNA is attached to the R strand at a unique site.
the DNA chain is growing from the 5’ end of the RNA.
